reason: The text depicts an Egyptian official (מִצְרִי - representing authority/elite) beating a Hebrew laborer (עִבְרִי - representing common people without power). Additionally, Pharaoh (the ultimate elite authority) actively seeks to kill Moses in response to the killing of the Egyptian, demonstrating the state using violence against perceived threats. The phrase describing Moses observing the Hebrews 'in their burdens' (בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם) contextualizes this as part of systematic oppression of regular people by those in power.
